rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nepal protects its biodiversity through 10 national parks (Chitwan, Bardia, Banke, Shuklaphanta, Koshi Tappu, Parsa, Ranipurna, Sagarmatha, Langtang, Annapurna, Makalu), 6 conservation areas (Kanchenjunga, Manaslu, etc.), 1 hunting reserve, and Ramsar wetlands. Chitwan (1973) and Sagarmatha (1976) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Chitwan National Park (1973) is the FIRST and most famous; it is home to the Bengal tiger and one-horned rhino.  ·  Sagarmatha National Park (1976) includes Mount Everest; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects Nepal's national parks, conservation areas, and Ramsar sites listed.  ·  IUCN categories (7) with examples is a very common exam question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: National parks: Chitwan (tiger, rhino), Sagarmatha (Everest), Langtang, Annapurna, Makalu, Kanchenjunga.  ·  Ramsar sites: Koshi Tappu, Rara, Chitwan Terai.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: IUCN "CR" = Critically Endangered (highest risk); "EN" = Endangered; "VU" = Vulnerable.  ·  A national park is more strictly protected (no human habitation) than a conservation area (allows local people inside).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nepal: 10 national parks, 6 conservation areas, 1 hunting reserve, Ramsar wetlands.  ·  Chitwan (1973): first park; Bengal tiger + one-horned rhino; UNESCO World Heritage.  ·  Sagarmatha (1976): Everest; UNESCO World Heritage.  ·  IUCN: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Chitwan National Park (1985) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the first Nepali park.  ·  The one-horned rhino (Rhinoceros unicornis) is found ONLY in Nepal and India.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Protected areas: designated areas for conservation; in Nepal: 10 national parks, 6 conservation areas, 1 hunting reserve, and Ramsar wetlands.  ·  National parks: Chitwan (1973, Bengal tiger + one-horned rhino), Bardia, Banke, Shuklaphanta, Koshi Tappu, Parsa, Rara, Langtang (1976), Sagarmatha (1976), Annapurna (1986), Manaslu (1986), Makalu (1992), Kanchenjunga (1989). NEB commonly cites 10 national parks; several sources list 11–14 depending on inclusion of the newer parks.  ·  Conservation areas (6): Kanchenjunga, Manaslu, Shey-Phoksundo, Khoratadi, Khaptad, and Barun.

rows.text: CITES  ·  Community forestry  ·  Endangered in Nepal: tiger (EN), rhino (VU), snow leopard (VU), elephant (EN), red panda (VU).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Causes of extinction: habitat loss, poaching, pollution, climate change, invasive species.  ·  Strategies: in-situ, ex-situ, community forestry, anti-poaching, CITES, awareness.  ·  Ramsar sites are internationally important WETLANDS (not the same as national parks).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Community forests (in-situ) and national parks are BOTH conservation strategies; they differ in management (community vs government).  ·  The one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) is VU (Vulnerable) globally; the Bengal tiger is EN (Endangered).  ·  Causes of extinction: habitat loss (deforestation), poaching, pollution, climate change, invasive species.
